research_mode: official Office for National Statistics and Police.uk sources only; current March 2026 crime guide, CSEW and police-recorded-crime scope, counting and QA rules, location and stop-search API contracts, and Crime Severity Score methodology; no parcel result or safety score claimed

sources.name: User guide to crime statistics for England and Wales: March 2026
verified_claims: the March 2026 user guide was last revised on 23 July 2026
ONS primarily uses CSEW and police recorded crime
the two sources have different strengths and limitations and are intended to be used together
limitations: complementary sources are not interchangeable measures
neither source supplies exact parcel evidence

sources.name: CSEW population coverage
verified_claims: CSEW interviews people aged 16 and over resident in households
it excludes group residences and other institutions
it does not cover crime against commercial or public-sector bodies
limitations: household survey coverage is not a full-population crime inventory
institutional and business victimisation require separate evidence

sources.name: CSEW geographic-purpose contract
verified_claims: the primary purpose of CSEW is national-level estimates
some headline figures are available at regional level
the survey is not designed as an exact small-area census
limitations: regional availability does not support LSOA or parcel assignment
sample estimates retain uncertainty

sources.name: CSEW long-term trend role
verified_claims: for covered crime types and populations CSEW includes crimes not reported to police
it is less affected by changes in police reporting and recording practices
its core victimisation approach supports long-term trend analysis
limitations: the advantage applies only to covered crimes and populations
survey-method changes and sampling uncertainty still require versioning

sources.name: CSEW 2025 to 2026 achieved sample and response
verified_claims: year ending March 2026 estimates use 31,350 face-to-face interviews
preliminary analysis reports a 48 percent adult response rate
weighting adjusts for possible non-response bias but estimates remain uncertain
limitations: weighting cannot prove absence of all non-response bias
survey estimates are not exact counts

sources.name: CSEW high-crime-area boost design
verified_claims: the 2025 to 2026 design included a 5,900-interview high-crime-area boost
English high-crime areas used the Index of Deprivation Crime Domain
Welsh areas used the Community Safety Index
limitations: sampling strata do not create parcel safety scores
the boost must be reflected in survey weights

sources.name: CSEW police-force-area sample design
verified_claims: the design targets at least 585 adult interviews in each of 42 territorial PFAs
City of London PFA is merged with Metropolitan PFA for analysis
PFA estimates are sample-based
limitations: PFA sampling does not support parcel inference
merged analytical areas must be retained in comparisons

sources.name: Police recorded crime coverage and local role
verified_claims: police data include institutions tourists commercial bodies and victimless offences outside CSEW scope
police data are the primary source of local crime statistics
they miss crimes not reported to or recorded by police
limitations: local availability is not parcel precision
recorded counts are affected by reporting recording and police activity

sources.name: Police recorded crime submission chain
verified_claims: returns cover 43 territorial forces plus British Transport Police
notifiable-offence data are supplied monthly to the Home Office
Home Office quality assurance precedes quarterly ONS preparation and publication
limitations: monthly submission does not imply immediate public completeness
BTP and territorial-force geographies differ

sources.name: Principal Crime Rule
verified_claims: England and Wales police-recorded crime is generally incident based
the Principal Crime Rule normally counts the most serious crime in a multi-crime incident
recorded offence counts are therefore not a count of every criminal act described
limitations: incident-based counts cannot be compared directly with multi-count systems
the rule has stated course-of-conduct exceptions

sources.name: Principal Crime Rule course-of-conduct exception
verified_claims: stalking harassment and controlling or coercive behaviour can be recorded as the principal course-of-conduct crime
this can take precedence over another more serious notifiable offence reported at the same time
the exception is rule-specific
limitations: offence hierarchy alone cannot reconstruct incident content
rule edition and offence context must be retained

sources.name: England and Wales versus Scotland counting systems
verified_claims: England and Wales normally record one principal crime in the example incident
Scottish rules would generally record individual crimes separately
identical events can therefore generate different counts
limitations: cross-jurisdiction counts require harmonised definitions
raw totals must not be compared without counting-rule adjustment

sources.name: Home Office police data validation
verified_claims: forces make automated monthly record-level submissions to HODH
Home Office validation checks query outliers with forces
forces may resubmit corrected data
limitations: validation does not audit whether all reportable crimes were recorded
extract versions can legitimately change after resubmission

sources.name: Crime trend data quality framework
verified_claims: ONS uses a data-quality framework for crime-type trend sources
trend reliability is classified as good moderate or poor
police-recorded-crime ratings consider recording-practice and police-activity changes
limitations: a crime-type trend rating is not row-level confidence
ratings do not establish parcel accuracy

sources.name: CSEW incidence and prevalence definitions
verified_claims: incidence counts the number of victimisation events per person or household
prevalence records whether victimisation occurred once or more
the measures have different denominators and interpretations
limitations: incidence and prevalence cannot be substituted
neither is a parcel probability

sources.name: CSEW self-completion offence measurement
verified_claims: ONS does not produce incidence rates for domestic abuse sexual assault and stalking
self-completion questions focus on whether a person was victimised
these outputs are prevalence measures rather than event counts
limitations: prevalence cannot estimate repeat-event volume
sensitive-offence measures require their separate survey context

sources.name: Rural and urban crime analysis geography
verified_claims: ONS crime analysis uses the recommended rural and urban method
below-local-authority data use the ONS rural and urban definition
when local authority is the lowest geography the LA classification is used
limitations: the two classifications are not interchangeable
classification does not provide parcel crime evidence

sources.name: Crime statistics table conventions
verified_claims: 0 can denote a non-zero percentage below 0.5 percent
x can denote not applicable not asked or unavailable depending on source
u and c denote low-base non-reporting and disclosure suppression contexts
limitations: symbols require table-specific definitions
symbols must not be converted to numeric zero

sources.publisher: Police.uk / Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: Crimes at a location API contract
verified_claims: location_id returns crimes mapped to that published location
latitude and longitude requests find the nearest predefined location
the method does not return every crime within a radius
limitations: nearest published location is not exact parcel matching
published locations remain anonymised approximations

sources.publisher: Police.uk / Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: Police.uk Scotland coverage warning
verified_claims: Police.uk warns location-search implementers about Scotland coverage
only British Transport Police supplies Scottish data to this service
displayed Scottish crime levels can therefore appear much lower than reality
limitations: absence of territorial Scottish force data is not zero crime
the slot's England scope must remain explicit

sources.publisher: Police.uk / Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: Stop and searches by area API
verified_claims: stop searches can be queried within one mile of a point or a custom polygon
returned locations are approximations rather than exact stop locations
point and polygon modes have different geometry
limitations: stop-search activity is not a crime-incidence measure
approximate locations cannot bind to parcels

sources.publisher: Police.uk / Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: Stop-search polygon transport limit
verified_claims: GET requests longer than 4094 characters return HTTP 400
complex polygon requests should use POST
transport method affects whether a valid area request is accepted
limitations: HTTP 400 is not evidence of no records
POST success still requires semantic and date validation

sources.publisher: Police.uk / Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: Stop-search date contract
verified_claims: date is optional and uses YYYY-MM
the latest month is returned by default
default results change as new months are published
limitations: reproducible use requires an explicit month
latest does not mean complete for every force

sources.publisher: Police.uk / Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: Stop-search datetime precision
verified_claims: some forces provide only dates for stop searches
date-only records can appear at midnight
midnight clustering can therefore be an artefact of source precision
limitations: midnight must not be interpreted as exact event time
force-level timestamp quality varies

sources.publisher: Police.uk / Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: Stop-search outcome missing semantics
verified_claims: outcome can be false when nothing was found
an empty string means no outcome was provided
these states have different meanings
limitations: false and empty must not be collapsed
outcome text is not a parcel risk value

sources.publisher: Police.uk / Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: Stop-search outcome linkage field
verified_claims: outcome_linked_to_object_of_search is boolean when supplied
null means the linkage was not provided
null is distinct from false
limitations: missing linkage cannot be inferred
the field describes stop-search outcome relation not crime severity

sources.name: Crime Severity Score purpose
verified_claims: Crime Severity Score is a weighted measure of police-recorded crime
it combines offence volume and relative severity
severity is intended to reflect societal harm and likely police demand
limitations: it is a police-recorded-crime measure
it is not a direct victim-harm or parcel-safety probability

sources.name: Crime Severity Score offence-weight formula
verified_claims: weights combine custody rate times average custodial sentence
community-order rate is multiplied by a guideline-based equivalency
fine rate is multiplied by an average-fine equivalency
limitations: weights reflect sentencing methodology rather than observed parcel harm
changes in sentencing policy require version control

sources.name: Crime Severity Score sentencing limitations
verified_claims: some sentencing outcomes are excluded from offence weights
life sentences require aggregate served-length assumptions
offences with no usable sentencing data can use a similar-offence proxy weight
limitations: proxy and aggregate assumptions reduce offence-specific directness
the methodology is not a raw observed severity scale

sources.name: Crime Severity Score denominator and maintenance limitations
verified_claims: weighted incidents are divided by mid-year resident population
the denominator excludes transient population
weights were intended for five-year updates across the time series and scores remain affected by police recording practices
limitations: resident population can misrepresent commuter or visitor exposure
recording changes can alter severity trends without equivalent underlying-crime change
